events.detail: From 0.27 in 1992 to 0.48 in 1997. Derived by detecting a sustained shift of at least 0.2 index points over 5 years; marked at the steepest year of the episode.
events.contested: V-Dem indices are aggregated expert judgements with published uncertainty intervals. A shift of this size is well outside the noise, but the exact year is a property of the detection rule, not a documented event.

events.title: Baht float triggers the Asian financial crisis
events.detail: After months of defending the peg and depleting reserves, Thailand floated the baht, which fell sharply; an IMF programme followed in August.
events.contested: The trigger point of a regional crisis. The debate over whether the cause was crony capitalism and weak balance sheets or panic and premature capital-account liberalisation reshaped mainstream thinking on capital controls.
events.refs: ["Bank of Thailand announcement, 2 July 1997", "Radelet & Sachs, 'The East Asian Financial Crisis' (1998)"]
